title: C = A @ B transposed
starter:
%A   = buffer 6 dtype=i32 slot=0
%B   = buffer 6 dtype=i32 slot=1
%C   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=2
# A is 2x3, B is 2x3, both row-major. C (2x2) = A @ B^T:
# C[i*2+j] = sum over k of A[i*3+k] * B[j*3+k]
# The starter indexes B as if it were 3x2 (plain A @ B).
%i   = range 2
%j   = range 2
%i2  = mul %i 2
%ij  = add %i2 %j
%cv  = shrink %C %ij shape=[]
%z   = store %cv 0
%C0  = after %C %z
%k   = range 3
%i3  = mul %i 3
%ik  = add %i3 %k
%av  = shrink %A %ik shape=[]
%a   = load %av
%k2  = mul %k 2
%kj  = add %k2 %j
%bv  = shrink %B %kj shape=[]
%b   = load %bv
%p   = mul %a %b
%cv0 = shrink %C0 %ij shape=[]
%cur = load %cv0
%sum = add %cur %p
%s   = store %cv0 %sum
%ek  = end %s %k
%ej  = end %ek %j
%ei  = end %ej %i
%C1  = after %C %ei
hints: Only one view is wrong. Which matrix is stored differently from plain A @ B?
In A @ B^T, row j of B plays the role of column j. Element k of that row sits at `j*3 + k`.
Replace `%k2 = mul %k 2` and `%kj = add %k2 %j` with `%j3 = mul %j 3` and `%jk = add %j3 %k`, and use `%jk` as B's offset. The bounds check still passes: j*3 + k is in [0, 5].
explain: With B transposed, the inner loop walks row j of B, at `j*3 + k`, instead of column j at `k*2 + j`. Both are provably in [0, 5], so both pass the bounds check, and only the test values tell them apart. The reset store depends on i and j through its offset, so it runs once per output element.
